is split into a multilingual training set and into multiple test sets to evaluate zero-shot cross-lingual and cross-target transfer.

In addition, multilingual Bert can generalize to a degree both cross-lingually and in a cross-target setting.

Baseline Experiments ::: Multilingual BERT Baseline ::: Results	Table TABREF36 shows the results for the cross-lingual setting.

Similar to the cross-lingual setting, M-Bert performs worse in a cross-target setting but easily surpasses the majority class baselines.

While the effect is negligible in most settings, the cross-lingual performance clearly increases when all questions are

The effect of missing questions is especially strong in the supervised and cross-lingual settings.

An M-Bert model that learns target embeddings instead of encoding a question performs clearly worse in the supervised and cross-lingual settings.

On the other hand, in the cross-lingual and cross-target settings, the mean score drops by 6–8 percentage points compared to the supervised setting; while zero-shot transfer is possible to a degree, it can still be improved.
